newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA READY TO SEIZE THEIR CHANCE AS JUVENTUS SLIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA READY TO SEIZE THEIR CHANCE AS JUVENTUS SLIP.

text.p: If Juventus believed they had the serie A title all sewn up, their chief rivals had a very different message for them on Monday.
Parma and Inter Milan both closed the gap on the reigning champions when Juventus crashed to an unexpected 3-0 home defeat to Udinese on Sunday.
Parma had their first ever victory over Roma in Rome, 1-0, while Internazionale beat AC Milan 3-1 in the Milan derby.
Those results left Juventus top with 52 points, Parma second on 49 and Inter third on 45. All three have seven matches left to play.
Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti is already looking forward to his side's scheduled meeting with Juventus in Turin on May 25.
"The game that may well decide the championship is the one in Turin. We'd better start thinking about it from now..."
Ancelotti is the first to admit his surprise at finding his side in the thick of the championship battle after an autumn when Parma sank close to the relegation zone and his own job was under threat.
"At first, we were looking at getting into third place, Juventus seemed unstoppable. Now, though, we're looking at the number one spot and we'd better keep our guard up", he said.

Juventus coach Marcello Lippi had difficulty explaining his side's collapse in a week that also saw the Turin club register emphatic away wins against Milan (6-1) and Ajax Amsterdam (2-1) in the Champions League.
"It's been a very special week for us and we've burned up a lot to win two remarkable games and probably we've paid for that", said Lippi.
Rather than criticise his players after the Udinese defeat, Lippi told them all to take two days off in preparation for next Saturday's away match at Bologna.
Inter's win over Milan was further bad news for Juventus as it confirmed Inter's current good form, coming just five days after their 3-1 UEFA Cup semifinal first-leg win against French side Monaco.

The win prompted Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson to admit that the club still had two objectives in their sights -- the UEFA Cup final and second place in serie A to earn a place in next season's expanded Champions League.
"There's no doubt that this win leaves us still in there with a chance of second place and it would be wrong not to go for both objectives while they are still possible," he said.
On Saturday, Inter are away to relegation battlers Cagliari while Parma are at home to Udinese.
The Italian media were united in their message for Juventus on Monday -- the title race has been blown wide open.

"K.O. For Juventus, The Championship Race Opens Up Again", said the front-page headline in Rome's daily La Repubblica, echoed by another Rome daily Il Messaggero which read, "Juventus Crumble, Udinese Open Up The Title Race."
